prerequisites: Having fully approved the basic training module, especially Linear Algebra, Calculus, Numerical Methods, Statistics, Waves and Electromagnetism, Graphic Expression and Fundamentals of Computer Science.

Having fully approved the common module to the industrial branch, especially the three subjects of Electricity, Electronics and Automation (Electronic Technology, Electrical Technology and Automation and Control).
Having approved the subject of Digital Electronic Systems.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic principles of electronic power conversion, basic configurations, and switching, conversion, and control elements.
Properly use specific computer programs for electronic circuit simulation and specific laboratory equipment.
Analyze and design power electronic circuits.
Select the most suitable electronic components and basic configuration for a given application.
Know and apply the regulations that power electronic equipment must comply with.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Power Electronics: Scope and utility, specific problems, available tools (mathematical and software).
Basic power topologies for energy conversion: DC/DC, AC/DC, AC/AC and DC/AC.
Power electronic devices: Non-ideality of semiconductor switches, electrical and thermal protection of semiconductors, association of power semiconductors.
Passive power devices: Coils, transformers, capacitors and resistors.
Basic applications of power electronics: loads and sources.
Overview of the course and work methodology
Presentation of the WRE, WED and WNA workshops
Projects of the Renewable Energy Workshop (WRE)
Projects of the Electronic Drives Workshop (WED)
Projects of the Nautical Applications Workshop (WNA)
Learning to formulate and specify a Power Electronics system
Non-ideality of semiconductor switches
Electrical and thermal protection of power semiconductors
Association of power semiconductors
DC/DC conversions
AC/DC conversions
AC/AC conversions
DC/AC conversions
Coils
Transformers
Group activity TG1 - Resolution of doubts and presentation of works (if applicable).
Basic handling of the power simulator: Installation and familiarization with the simulation environment that will be used in successive practices.
Introduction to the Buck converter
PWM signal generation and basic module creation with the simulator
Basic Buck converter with PWM module
Introduction to digital control modules in power systems. Implementation of state machines in the simulator
Basic Buck converter with PWM module and basic digital control.
Switch branches. "Bootstrap" technique for branch control. Introduction to the use of commercial integrated circuits. Library management.
Complete Buck converter based on a switch branch. Use of the "Bootstrap" technique with a commercial integrated circuit.
DC-DC Buck-Boost and Flyback converter.
Transformers in LTSPice.
Evolution of the Buck-Boost converter towards the Flyback
Modeling of solar panels in the simulator.
Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) system in a solar panel.
The Flyback converter as an equivalent voltage at the input of the solar panel.
Implementation of a quasi-MPPT control
Control in current mode (Imax-Min). Charging a 12 V battery from a 48 V Bus
Option 1: Buck in current mode.
Basic state machine of Imax-Imin control
Option 2: Evolution towards the Forward converter in current mode
Learning to generate control signals. Full-bridge DC-DC converter
Push-Pull control.
Push-Pull control and phase shift control.
Square wave inverters. Signal generation by phase shift for controlling two full bridges with variable frequency and duty cycle and controlled phase shift between them.
Single-phase voltage mode inverter (VMI) with SPWM modulation.
teaching_methods: Workrooms (Renewable Energy, Electronic Drives, Nautical Applications)

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical exam with exercises and problems

assessment_rules: A minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required on the theoretical exam. A minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required on the practical simulation exam. The practical exam can only be evaluated if the minimum grade on the theoretical exam has been obtained.
